chapter: Piano players, Hot Springs and Chicago
title: Chicago piano playing and musicians he heard there
summary: In Chicago he practiced piano where he stayed, heard Manny Jones and a cornetist on State Street, and discusses Joe Oliver and the Royal Gardens.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When you were in Chicago, did you have a regular job as solo piano player or what?
No, no, I just was playing at a, where I was stopping, they had a piano, and I just practiced on a piano every day, you know. Uh huh.
Did you meet any other New Orleans music piano players up in Chicago, except mine?
Well, no, no, I just met this fellow, Manny Jones. And I used to go and listen at, when I, book. You remember book? No.
Yeah. What block? He was playing at, in the 3300 block, State Street.
Is that near the Royal Gardens? No, the Royal Gardens, around? The Royal Gardens, around?
The Royal Gardens, around on, uh, 30th Street.
One-eyed buck. You mean bad-eyed Joe? Joe? He's, he's the fellow that sent for the, that's Louis Armstrong. That'd be Joe Oliver.
Joe Oliver, that's his name. Yeah, yeah. One-eyed buck. One-eyed buck. I never heard a guy. I heard a bad-eyed Joe, but never one. One-eyed buck. Mm- dear
